articles.description:
AI travel as a sector heated up in 2023, crowded in 2024, and started shutting down in 2025. I've watched AI travel products on the market. More died than survived. And the failure reasons are suspiciously consistent. They all died in the same spot.
This post breaks down five typical failure cases. How did they die? A warning for founders entering this space.
First case, the most common type: AI itinerary tool. User inputs destination, days, budget. AI generates a full plan. Sounds nice.
I've seen ten-plus of these. Most died. Why?
Because they only did "generate the itinerary." After generating, then what? The plan says "Day 1: visit the Forbidden City." User books tickets themselves. It says "stay near Wangfujing at night." User books a hotel themselves. It says "eat at this restaurant."…

articles.author: Mohammad Mostafazadeh
articles.description:
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) adoption in non-Western markets frequently faces a severe bottleneck: native ERP engines are deeply hardcoded around the Gregorian calendar, Latin typography, and Western accounting conventions. In countries like Iran and Afghanistan, where official business records strictly require the Solar Hijri (Jalali / Shamsi) calendar and right-to-left (RTL) localization, running a standard ERP implementation often turns into an engineering nightmare.
Historically, localization teams made the fatal mistake of forking the upstream source code or creating parallel database engines. When upstream releases a major version (e.g., Odoo 17 to Odoo 18, and now Odoo 19), forked implementations break catastrophically.
The engineering team at Abrak Cloud ERP pioneered an alternative architectural approach: pure non-destructive extension (_inherit). By implementing dual-layer conversion adapters, the database persists dates in standard UTC ISO format, while the web client (OWL/JavaScript) and report rendering engines translate date projections on the fly using high-precision algorithms.
Precision Solar Hijri Engine: Full leap-year precision conforming to the 33-year astronomical cycle, available via the Jalali Calendar Odoo 19 framework.
Direct Electronic Invoicing & Cryptographic Compliance: Automated generation of 22-digit cryptographic tax identifiers, canonical JSON payload assembly, and asymmetric RSA/ECC signing for national tax authority gateways.
Dedicated Database Isolation: Ensuring each enterprise tenant operates within an independent PostgreSQL database container, eliminating data co-mingling risks found in shared-tenant SaaS architectures.
Developers and international engineering teams interested in modern open-source enterprise software architecture can explore the comprehensive documentation and live sandboxes at abrak.org.
articles.title: Localizing Open-Source ERP: How Odoo 19 is Adapted for Solar Hijri, Complex Tax, and RTL

articles.author: suissAI
articles.description:
Executive Summary: Current AI assistants are mostly reactive: they wait for a user’s message, run the model, and answer. This works for simple queries but wastes the many idle cycles between interactions. In contrast, a truly proactive agent continuously monitors state, predicts future needs, and acts (or prompts the user) before being asked. Here we argue that instead of bolting on occasional webhooks or notifications, the entire architecture should be designed for proactivity. This “Proactive by Construction” approach minimizes wasted user-initiated messages and shifts heavy work into idle periods. 
We compare the reactive, event-driven architecture (e.g. waking on every email) with a state-driven proactive design. We detail how to build the latter using (1) persistent domain state and p…
articles.title: Proactive by Construction: Why the Next Generation of Agents Must Anticipate, Not Just React

articles.author: jidonglab
articles.description:
A user emailed me a screenshot of their feedback report. Under "Communication," my scoring model had written: "Closed the answer with 'Thanks for watching,' which feels scripted and out of place in a live conversation."
They never said it. They paused for about four seconds, decided they were done, and stopped talking. Whisper filled the silence for them, and then an LLM graded them on the words Whisper made up.
This post covers Whisper hallucinations on silence: how often they happened in my pipeline (9.2% of clips), why the built-in no_speech_threshold didn't catch them, and the config change that got the count from 183 to 4.
Whisper hallucinates text on silence. Trailing or leading quiet in a clip gets filled with phrases like "Thanks for watching!", "Thank you.", or "Subtitles by the A…
